title: What Andy Burnham can do about Palestine
gist: Prospect argues the new Burnham/Miliband UK government should pivot Israel-Palestine policy away from the Abraham Accords toward the 2002 Arab Peace Initiative, and use the UK's underused trade and defence leverage over Israel — starting with demanding a health update on and prison access to imprisoned Fatah leader Marwan Barghouti, the only Palestinian figure polling as a cross-faction unifier ahead of November Palestinian elections.

insights.claim: The UK and EU are Israel's most important trading partners but have deliberately left that economic leverage unused in the Israel-Palestine file, meaning a policy shift has real unexercised tools behind it.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Watch for UK/EU trade measures on Israel as the first concrete signal that rhetoric is becoming policy — a live risk to Israeli export and defence-tech names.
insights.quote: Neither the UK nor the EU have used much of the leverage available to them.
insights.locator: But if the new British government wants

insights.claim: The UK holds a separate Trade and Partnership Agreement with Israel plus a memorandum of understanding covering cyber security, technology, trade and defence — the specific instruments that would be suspended or renegotiated in any pressure campaign.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: The TPA and the cyber/defence MoU are the identifiable contract-level exposure for UK-Israel tech and defence cooperation.
insights.quote: They are both tremendously important trading partners for Israel.
insights.locator: But if the new British government wants to intervene

insights.claim: Requesting a health update on Palestinian security prisoners and a formal prison visit is presented as a costless first move for London precisely because refusal is expected — the value is precedent-setting and signalling, not access.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: A cheap, high-visibility diplomatic escalation ladder: watch for it as the leading indicator of a harder UK line before any trade action.
insights.locator: One thing that the Burnham government can do immediately

insights.claim: Engaging the incumbent Netanyahu government during Israel's election season is dismissed as pointless, implying UK policy will effectively be frozen until after the 27th October Israeli vote.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Sets a timing floor: expect no substantive UK-Israel diplomatic movement before late October 2026.
insights.quote: engaging with the current Netanyahu government—especially in election season—makes no sense

insights.claim: The Palestinian Authority has been stripped of remaining power by Netanyahu's government and is less popular than ever, leaving no institution capable of signing or enforcing an agreement.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Any peace framework priced on a PA counterparty is unfundable until a credible Palestinian executive exists.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the Palestinian Authority (PA) is less popular than ever

insights.claim: Mahmoud Abbas is 90 years old and functioning as a barely-caretaker leader, while his apparent hand-picked successor Hussein al-Sheikh polls below 3 per cent among Palestinians.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Succession risk is not hedged: the designated heir has no popular base, so a disorderly transition is the base case.
insights.quote: doesn’t register above 3 per cent in popularity among Palestinians
insights.locator: Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing government has stripped it

insights.claim: Palestinian legislative and presidential elections are scheduled for November 2026 — the first since 2006 — immediately after Israel's 27th October vote, creating a compressed two-month window in which both leaderships could change.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: A dated, two-sided political catalyst window for Middle East risk premia in Q4 2026.
insights.locator: Following the Israeli election, there will be Palestinian legislative

insights.claim: The Palestinian Authority was designed under the 1993 Oslo Accords as a temporary waystation to statehood, so its current decay is structural rather than a recent failure of leadership.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Frames PA collapse as institutional design reaching end-of-life, arguing against patch-up diplomacy.
insights.locator: The PA, set up by the 1993 Oslo Accords

insights.claim: Marwan Barghouti has led Palestinian polling across all factions — Fatah and Hamas supporters alike — for more than three years, making him the only figure with cross-ideological legitimacy to sign a deal.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Any credible negotiation track runs through Barghouti's release; his status is the single highest-leverage variable in the file.
insights.quote: Polling from the last more than three years shows Barghouti is the favourite among all factions.
insights.locator: As I previously wrote in Prospect

insights.claim: Barghouti, 66, is serving five life sentences plus 40 years and is actively considering a presidential run from prison, with a final decision contingent on an election date being announced.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: A prison candidacy announcement would be the concrete trigger event to watch in the November election cycle.
insights.locator: The 66-year-old is being held on five life sentences

insights.claim: Barghouti still publicly supports a two-state outcome and peace with Israel according to his published statements and family, which is what makes his release strategically interesting rather than merely humanitarian.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Distinguishes him from rejectionist alternatives — the reason Western capitals are quietly engaging.

insights.claim: His son Arab Barghouti reports the family has had no contact with Marwan for over three years except through a lawyer who must repeatedly demand access, alleging prolonged solitary confinement, torture, starvation and broken ribs.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Health deterioration is a tail risk that would remove the one unifying Palestinian candidate from the board entirely.
insights.quote: prolonged solitary confinement, torture, starvation, repeated assaults, and severe physical abuse, including broken ribs

insights.claim: Israel's Supreme Court has ordered far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir to permit International Red Cross visits to Israeli prisons, but no such visit has occurred since 7th October 2023 — a live non-compliance with both Israeli and international law.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: A documented rule-of-law gap that gives foreign governments a legally grounded pressure point.

insights.claim: Barghouti's cause has already been picked up by Macron, the Saudis and even Trump, alongside a UK-based campaign incubator, indicating his release is moving from fringe advocacy to mainstream diplomatic currency.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Rising international salience raises the probability of a negotiated release being tabled in Q4 talks.
insights.quote: the one inmate who may hold the key to a different future
insights.locator: Other world leaders have embraced Barghouti

themes.theme: Abraham Accords vs Arab Peace Initiative

insights.claim: The Arab Peace Initiative, first proposed by Saudi Arabia in 2002, offers Israel recognition from the broad swath of Arab nations in exchange for accepting a Palestinian state — the structural opposite of the Abraham Accords, which make no Palestinian demands on Israel.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Two competing normalisation architectures; which one a UK government backs determines whether Gulf-Israel commercial integration is conditioned on Palestinian statehood.
insights.quote: agreements under the Accords have made no demands on Israel regarding the Palestinians
insights.locator: Taking the Arab Peace Initiative out of the shadows

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia is the gatekeeper to the remaining Arab states' recognition of Israel, and remains consistent that it will not normalise without a Palestinian state — even when Trump dangled US nuclear capability as the price.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Saudi normalisation — a major regional capital-flow catalyst — is hard-blocked on Palestinian statehood; do not price it as imminent.
insights.quote: The Saudis remain consistent that they will not agree to normalisation with Israel without a Palestinian state.
insights.locator: Indeed, Trump recently waived this option again

insights.claim: The Trump-brokered Gaza plan does not require Hamas to disarm until Israel halts incursions, and Israel shows no sign of stopping — so the deal is a hidden stalemate that only Trump treats as a resolution.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Treat the Gaza 'peace plan' as unresolved: escalation risk is materially higher than headlines imply.
insights.quote: It’s a stalemate hidden by a Trump-blessed agreement that only the US president appears to think is a resolution
insights.locator: not to mention the war in Gaza

insights.claim: The Israeli public's core demand is a blanket security agreement with all Arab states, which is the lever that makes the Arab Peace Initiative saleable in Israeli domestic politics despite its Palestinian-statehood condition.
insights.speaker: Jo-Ann Mort
insights.so_what: Identifies the domestic Israeli demand curve any deal must satisfy — security-for-statehood, not land-for-peace.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia is the gatekeeper to the remaining countries
insights.locator: The Israeli public deeply desires a blanket agreement
